Now Q4:

**Question:** What should the preserved local copy of a saved page actually contain?

**Why it matters:** This drives how much storage the app uses and how faithful the offline copy is — a full-fidelity capture with images can be large, while a readable-text snapshot stays lightweight. It sets the acceptance test for US12/FR-025.

**Recommended:** Option B — a self-contained readable snapshot (the article text and essential inline images folded into a single saved file) survives link rot and stays legible offline without the storage cost and fragility of capturing every asset on the page. PDFs are always kept as the original file regardless of this choice.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | **Readable text only** — extract the main article text (and the preview image); smallest storage, loses page layout |
| B | **Self-contained readable snapshot** — main content plus its essential inline images embedded in one saved file; legible offline, moderate size |
| C | **Full-page capture** — the complete page with all assets/styling as it appeared; highest fidelity, largest storage, more capture failures |

You can reply with the option letter, accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.
